caption: Missing data is limited to three numerical columns at exactly 3% each and is scattered uniformly across the rows; only 6 rows lose more than one value.
The dataset is moderately imbalanced (30.4% active) and the activity label is a hard threshold on the binding affinity at exactly pKi = 7.0.
Applying the rule `active = 1 if binding_affinity >= 7.0` reproduces the label for 100% of the 2,000 rows, so the two targets encode the same information.
Binding affinity is unimodal and close to normal in the centre but carries a heavy right tail of high-affinity compounds that bends away from the Q-Q reference line.
Most descriptors are symmetric and bell-shaped; the count features are discrete, `protein_length` is uniform by construction, and `mw_ratio` is by far the most asymmetric feature.
After standardisation every feature is centred on zero; the length of each box shows that `mw_ratio` and the count features carry the most extreme tails.
Only `mw_ratio` exceeds the announced 5% outlier rate under the IQR rule, while a simple domain rule exposes a negative polar surface area that no statistical rule would necessarily flag.
Correlations are read on a diverging blue-to-red ramp whose neutral grey midpoint means zero; the feature block is almost uncorrelated, and only the two targets and the logP-derived terms stand out.

Only `logp_pi_interaction` and `logp` carry a strong signal towards both targets; every other descriptor sits near zero, so non-linear models will have to earn their advantage from interactions rather than from single features.
The six most associated features plotted against binding affinity: the two logP-derived terms trend strongly, `protein_pi` mildly, and the remaining three form featureless clouds.
Violin plots of every feature split by class, annotated with the Mann-Whitney U p-value; only `logp`, the shipped interaction term and `protein_pi` separate the two classes.
Each protein is screened against about five compounds only, so per-protein statistics are noisy and target encoding would overfit badly.
Most compounds respect the Rule of Five, yet the drug-like subset is markedly LESS active: potency here is driven by lipophilicity, which is exactly what the oral-bioavailability filters penalise.
The features are nearly orthogonal, so no small set of components summarises them, yet the two classes already separate along PC1, which the loadings show is the lipophilicity axis.
t-SNE on a 1,200-compound sample finds no isolated cluster of active compounds; high-affinity points are spread through the embedding.

Mutual information and effect size agree with the correlation analysis: the two logP terms dominate, `protein_pi` follows with a medium effect, and the remaining ten descriptors are statistically indistinguishable between the two classes.
4 engineered terms reach |r| >= 0.5, but none overtakes the interaction column shipped with the dataset, which stays the strongest single predictor.
